summary:
AstroBase: Moon & Mars Survival Simulator is an interactive 3D educational game designed to introduce young learners to the challenges of human space exploration. Developed in response to NASA Space Apps Challenge’s “Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer,” the project transforms space science into a hands-on learning experience where players explore lunar and Martian environments and make decisions to support astronaut survival.

AstroBase makes complex scientific concepts easier to understand by allowing learners to experience them through gameplay rather than simply reading about them in textbooks. By managing essential resources, responding to mission challenges, and making survival decisions, players learn why oxygen, water, energy, food, and radiation protection are critical for life beyond Earth. These interactive experiences encourage critical thinking, decision-making, and problem-solving while helping learners connect scientific knowledge with practical situations.

Our goal is to make space education more engaging, memorable, and accessible, inspiring the next generation of explorers to develop scientific curiosity and a deeper understanding of humanity's future beyond Earth.
details:
Project Details — AstroBase: Moon & Mars Survival Simulator

What Does the Project Do and How Does It Work?

AstroBase is an interactive, browser-based 3D educational survival simulator that introduces young learners to the challenges of human exploration and settlement beyond Earth. Players take on the role of an astronaut and experience survival missions in two different environments: the Moon and Mars.

The simulator features two campaigns: a 20-day Moon mission and a 30-day Mars mission. During each mission, players must manage five essential survival resources: power, water, food, oxygen, and radiation shielding. Mission events, environmental challenges, and decision-making scenarios require players to think carefully about how their choices affect the survival of their outpost.

Players can explore the 3D environment, collect resources, respond to mission situations, and complete objectives while monitoring their mission status. The experience also includes a safe-zone survival mechanic that introduces the importance of remaining within protected areas.

An AI-powered mission companion named NOVA provides contextual guidance, answers mission-related questions, and helps players explore space-science concepts during their journey.

Benefits and Educational Value

AstroBase aims to make space science more understandable through active participation rather than passive learning. Textbooks can explain concepts such as oxygen supply, radiation exposure, energy consumption, and resource limitations, but these ideas may be difficult for young learners to visualize or connect with real situations.

AstroBase gives learners an opportunity to experience these challenges through gameplay. By managing limited resources and observing the consequences of their decisions, players can better understand why each survival system matters.

The experience encourages:

  • Scientific curiosity and interest in space exploration.
  • Critical thinking and informed decision-making.
  • Problem-solving and resource-management skills.
  • Understanding of the environmental challenges of the Moon and Mars.
  • Learning through experimentation, feedback, and practical scenarios.

Instead of simply memorizing scientific facts, learners can apply concepts in a simulated mission environment, potentially making the learning experience more engaging and memorable.

Intended Impact

Our goal is to make space education more interactive, accessible, and engaging for the next generation of explorers. AstroBase connects classroom science with mission-inspired practical experiences, helping young learners develop a deeper understanding of the challenges astronauts may face beyond Earth.

We hope the project will encourage students to explore STEM subjects, ask questions about space science, and develop an interest in humanity's future in space. By presenting complex ideas through an accessible game-based experience, AstroBase aims to make space exploration feel less distant and more understandable.

Tools and Technologies Used

AstroBase was developed using a combination of web technologies, 3D graphics tools, and AI integration:

  • React: Building the interactive user interface and application components.
  • JavaScript: Implementing gameplay logic, mission systems, and interactive features.
  • Vite: Frontend development and build tooling.
  • Three.js and React Three Fiber: Creating and rendering the interactive 3D environments.
  • Node.js and Express: Supporting backend services and API integration.
  • Claude API: Powering NOVA, the AI-based mission companion.
  • NASA Open Data and space-science resources: Informing the project's space-related concepts and mission context.
  • GLB/glTF 3D assets: Supporting astronaut, spacecraft, rover, and outpost models.

The project is deployed as a web application so users can access the experience through a browser without installing a dedicated game application.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of AstroBase lies in combining 3D exploration, survival simulation, educational scenarios, and AI-assisted guidance into one learning experience.

Rather than presenting space science as a collection of facts, the project places learners inside mission-inspired situations where they must make decisions and experience their consequences. The separate Moon and Mars campaigns also introduce different mission durations and environmental challenges, encouraging learners to understand that survival strategies depend on the environment.

NOVA adds an interactive learning companion to the experience, allowing players to seek guidance and explore questions while progressing through their missions.

Factors Considered During Development

Our team considered several important factors while developing AstroBase:

  • Educational relevance: Keeping the gameplay connected to real space-science and astronaut-survival concepts.
  • Target audience: Making the experience approachable and engaging for young learners.
  • Scientific context: Reflecting important challenges of off-world living, including limited resources and environmental hazards.
  • Engagement: Combining exploration, mission events, objectives, and decision-making to maintain interest.
  • Accessibility: Developing a browser-based experience to reduce installation barriers.
  • Learning through consequences: Designing resource and survival systems so that player decisions have meaningful outcomes.
  • Future potential: Keeping the project open to further improvements in simulation depth, educational content, and immersive technologies.

AstroBase represents our team's effort to turn the challenges of future human space exploration into an engaging learning experience—where young explorers do not just read about survival beyond Earth, but get to experience the decisions behind it.
